cells.tense: You are handing strength outward right now, at the size the moment can take it.
cells.ask: Give one person something you already have spare, then stop and look at what the two of you can build with it next.
cells.core: You're holding your ground and handing pieces of it out at the same time. Not the loudest support in the room. Not a hand that grabs. You give at a size the other person can actually take, and passing it over doesn't empty you.\n\nHere's the part that's easy to miss. What you put into someone's hands tends to show in what they can do after they leave you, not only in what you passed across. You stop dimming what you can carry. You offer it at the size it really is. Someone else's afternoon opens up a little. That isn't a metaphor. It's a way of moving through a room, and it's happening now.
cells.sheetLine: You share at a size the other person can hold, and it doesn't empty you.

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future in which the people you support fall apart without you.
cells.ask: Find one thing you're carrying for somebody else, put it down for a full day, and watch what they do without it.
cells.core: You're carrying weight that hasn't been handed to you yet. Somebody might need this later, so you're already bracing under the shape of it. That has gone past generosity. It has become preparation for a crisis that keeps not arriving while you keep getting stronger and more tired.\n\nWhat you give has stopped being something you offer and become something you enforce. You decide what people need before they've asked, and you pass it over whether or not the moment calls for it. That isn't generous anymore. That's control wearing a generous coat, and you can feel what it costs. The people you help don't get to find their own footing, because yours is already in the way.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying weight nobody asked you to lift yet.

cells.tense: You stopped offering what you have, and the door you are still standing at is already shut.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you know that would help them, even badly, and let that be enough for today.
cells.core: You have strength to share and the sharing isn't happening. Not because you're empty. The offering stopped, and you've kept what you have in your own hands ever since. Sitting on it can feel safe. It isn't. When you don't offer, you're absent from a place where your strength would have made the difference.\n\nYour body is here. Your support isn't. It stopped at a threshold you crossed and haven't walked back through since. What you have to give is intact. What stalled is the simplest part: saying to somebody, here, take this, it's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You have strength to share and the offering stalled.

cells.tense: You are already the one people steady themselves against, and you are calling it nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Tell one person, plainly, that you're the one holding this together, then say nothing more about it.
cells.core: You're the structure people lean on and you describe it like it happened on its own. Not as a choice. Not as a strength. As just what's going on, who knows why. But you're the one who decided to carry it, and you're the one who shares it at that particular size. It's running, and it belongs to somebody.\n\nYou don't need to be grand about it. You could stop acting like the support you give showed up by itself. The moment you claim the load as your own call, something settles. Not pride. Just the pen back in the hand that was already holding it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one holding it. You're calling it just what's happening.
